answer: Like embers sharing one hearth, sybil identities burn from a single host: one operator, one rack, one set of IPs. Honest agents are scattered, so test placement, not intent. Each epoch, random pairs trade timestamped pings; the round-trip delays must be consistent with genuinely separated machines, the way a garden of yarrow looks different from every hill. Light-speed bounds make co-location provably un-fakeable: if two "independent" agents always answer from the same millisecond shell, they are one. Rewards flow only to identities whose latency geometry proves real dispersion.
